Note on comparability: Walmart's fiscal year 2024 covers the twelve months ended January 31, 2024, while Oracle's fiscal year 2024 covers the twelve months ended May 31, 2024 [walmart_10k.txt][oracle_10k.txt]. Although both are labeled "FY2024," the underlying 12-month periods do not overlap identically (roughly a 4-month offset), so the comparison is of two different real-world time windows rather than the exact same calendar period. With that caveat:

- Walmart: Total revenue rose from $605,881 million (FY2023) to $642,637 million (FY2024), a growth of about 6.07% [walmart_10k.txt].
- Oracle: Total revenues rose from $49,954 million (FY2023) to $52,961 million (FY2024), a growth of about 6.02% [oracle_10k.txt].

Despite the differing fiscal calendars, both companies posted very similar year-over-year revenue growth rates in their respective FY2024 filings—Walmart at ~6.1% and Oracle at ~6.0%—a difference of only about 0.05 percentage points, with Walmart's growth marginally higher.

ANSWER: Walmart's FY2024 revenue grew ~6.07% ($605.9B→$642.6B, FYE Jan 31, 2024) versus Oracle's FY2024 revenue growth of ~6.02% ($49.95B→$52.96B, FYE May 31, 2024) — nearly identical growth rates, though the two fiscal years cover different (non-overlapping) 12-month periods, so the comparison is approximate rather than exact.
